title: Response-format multiplexer and graceful schema fallback for OpenAI-compat
author: Dina Patel
release_notes: Add response_format negotiation layer that multiplexes streaming and non-streaming validation paths; when strict schema mode triggers in-stream schema violations, requests automatically fall back to a non-streaming validation run which returns structured schema diagnostics in OpenAI-compat format. Backwards-compatible for existing clients; opt-in strict behavior via response_format.strict=true.
description: Motivation: customers need predictable structured-output validation while keeping streaming latency benefits. Previously strict schema checks caused opaque aborts or dropped streams in the OpenAI compatibility layer. This change introduces a response-format multiplexer that: (1) negotiates response_format and schema metadata from user request and OpenAI-compat parameters; (2) runs an optimized in-stream schema validator that is permissive by default but can operate in strict mode; (3) if strict validation fails during streaming, transparently falls back to a non-streaming re-render validation pass and returns a detailed OpenAI-compat error payload instead of a truncated stream. Key user-visible behaviors: - response_format now accepts an object-style shorthand (e.g. {"type":"json_schema","strict":true}) in addition to legacy strings. - Streaming path will attempt in-flight validation and continue where safe; if a violation is detected in strict mode we stop the stream and switch to a synchronous validation run that returns complete schema diagnostics. - OpenAI-compat errors created on fallback follow the shape: {"error":{"message":"schema validation failed","type":"invalid_response","param":"response_format","code":"schema_violation","details":[...]}} , and we set a finish_reason of "schema_violation" on the compatibility envelope. - Function/tool-calling runtime is updated to buffer function args when response_format.strict is set to avoid partial side-effects if validation fails. Implementation summary: - core: add response_format multiplexer and canonicalizer (src/respfmt/multiplexer.py). - streaming: in-flight validator with size-limited buffer and heuristics for safe continuation (src/inference/streaming_validator.py). - compat: map internal schema diagnostics to OpenAI error envelope and finish_reason (src/openai_compat/response_mapper.py). - runtime: small orchestration layer to attempt streaming first, then re-run a deterministic non-streaming render with the same model checkpoint and prompt history if needed (src/runtime/negotiator.py). - tests: unit + e2e covering permissive streaming, strict fail->fallback path, function-call buffering, and backwards compatibility with string response_format (tests/test_respformat_mux.py, tests/e2e_openai_compat_schema.py). Backwards compatibility notes: most clients are unaffected; clients using the new object-style response_format will opt in to stricter semantics. Performance: streaming latency path unchanged for permissive mode; strict-mode fallback adds an extra synchronous validation pass on failure (documented in release notes). Security and safety: function-call buffering prevents external side-effects before schema confirmation. Migration: document new response_format shape in docs/openai_compat_response_format.md and add SDK examples in redwood-sdk-python and ts. Checklist: - implemented multiplexer and negotiator; - added in-stream validator and fallback logic; - safety: buffered function/tool-call behavior validated; - tests and docs updated; - benchmarked common permissive streaming path to confirm <3% p99 latency regression.

review_thread: Marco Li: Please add more unit coverage around partial-token boundaries for the in-stream validator.
Dina Patel: Added tests for token boundary conditions and updated heuristics to avoid false positives.
Asha Reddy: Functional buffering looks good; can you confirm effects on long-running function calls?

Dina Patel: Buffering only delays function argument emission until post-validate; long-running functions are unaffected because we only buffer args not invocation triggers in permissive mode. Added note in docs.
Jon Collins: CI flagged lint on the first run; re-run fixed after style tweaks.
Marco Li: Approved after addressing unit tests and adding the openai-compat doc example.
notes: This PR intentionally preserves legacy string response_format for compatibility. Teams that require strict validation should opt into the object-style response_format. We added telemetry counters: respfmt.fallback.count and respfmt.strict_violation.count to help monitor fallback frequency. If fallback rate exceeds 1% for a customer, ops will surface recommended prompt/schema changes.
